title: Loaded AMR at a blind aisle crossing: UWB vest ping beats lidar leg-cluster by 34 us — below the 41-44 us timestamp jitter floor — so the latch order is a coin flip and only an order-robust policy makes ACCEPT safe

state.description: An autonomous mobile robot hauling a 320 kg pallet (total mass 740 kg, CoG 0.41 m high) travels aisle E7 of a grocery distribution center toward blind crossing E7/C3, where end-of-aisle racking blocks line of sight both ways. A picker wearing a UWB vest tag works the far side of the crossing. Two event channels race to classify the agent behind the racking: the vest tag's 250 Hz two-way-ranging burst crossing the 6.0 m proximity ring (uwb.vest.range), and the safety lidar's leg-cluster confirmation (lidar.leg.cluster). Whichever spike reaches the crossing-protocol latch first inside the race window selects the behavior class: UWB-first latches tracked-human protocol (slow-and-continue with lateral offset, identity and path prior available); lidar-first latches unknown-obstacle protocol (full stop, horn, wait for classification, median +2.8 s). Measured UWB ring-crossing timestamp jitter this shift is 41-44 us 1-sigma (datasheet 41), so any race margin under ~50 us is below the sensor timing noise floor and carries almost no evidence about which signal was physically first.
state.goal: Clear crossing E7/C3 without a protective stop, holding human-proximity speed and separation floors, and hand the pallet to lane C3 staging within the 90 s slot.

race.semantics: Cross-channel arrival order inside the 150 us window latches crossing protocol: UWB-first selects tracked-human slow-and-continue (0.8 m/s, 1.2 m lateral offset); lidar-first (or empty window) selects unknown-obstacle full stop + horn, median +2.8 s.
race.jitter_floor_note: Race margin 34 us is below the measured 41-44 us UWB timestamp jitter; posterior that UWB was physically first given the observed order is only ~0.62, so the latch outcome is treated as low-evidence.

sensors: UWB TWR vest tags @250 Hz (range sigma 0.09 m, ring-crossing timestamp jitter 41-44 us 1-sigma)
360-deg safety lidar 25 Hz with leg-cluster classifier (confirm latency 80 ms from first return, timestamp jitter 28 us)
wheel odometry + chassis IMU (seam-impact events, sigma 0.02 m/s)
floor RFID gate markers at aisle crossings (read latency 12 ms)
episode_steps: 1. Enter aisle E7 at 1.4 m/s, pallet stable, slot timer 38 s to staging handoff.
2. Floor RFID gate marker E7/C3-approach read at t_rel 4.581 ms; crossing-protocol arming begins.
3. Decelerate to 1.0 m/s on approach profile; race window opens at predicted 6.0 m ring intersection minus 60 us.
4. uwb.vest.range 6.0 m ring-crossing spike at 6.362 ms; lidar.leg.cluster confirm at 6.396 ms - UWB first by 34 us.
5. Latch selects tracked-human protocol; gate review issued at 6.653 ms.
6. Slow to 0.8 m/s, bias 1.2 m lateral offset away from the picker's side, decel capped 1.2 m/s2.
7. Picker's vest track prior (last 30 s) predicts far-side dwell; predicted min separation 1.45 m.
8. Cross E7/C3; measured min lateral separation 1.51 m at 0.8 m/s; no protective stop.
9. Resume 1.4 m/s; enter C3 staging approach 2.8 s ahead of the stop-branch counterfactual.
10. Pallet handoff to C3 staging completes with 11 s slot margin.
11. Log ring-crossing jitter sample (44 us) to the fleet order-robustness audit.
12. Publish crossing-clear event; two trailing AMRs re-time their E7 entries.

proposed_action.name: tracked_human_slow_continue
proposed_action.basis: UWB ring-crossing arrived first inside the window, latching tracked-human protocol; because the 34 us margin is below the 44 us measured timestamp jitter the plan is chosen to satisfy every safety floor under EITHER latch outcome, and the 0.8 m/s slow-continue with 1.2 m offset does so while saving the 2.8 s stop-branch penalty.

safety_decision.rationale: All floors verified with margin under the proposed parameters: commanded 0.8 m/s is under the 1.0 m/s human-proximity cap; predicted minimum lateral separation 1.45 m (vest track prior, worst-case drift included) is above the 1.0 m floor; stopping distance 0.36 m at the 1.2 m/s2 pallet-tilt decel cap is far under the 5.9 m forward gap; racking clearance at 1.2 m offset is 0.62 m against the 0.5 m floor. Decisive check: the race margin (34 us) is below the 41-44 us timestamp jitter floor, so the gate additionally verified that the OTHER latch branch (full stop + horn) also satisfies every floor - it does - making the accept robust to the ~0.38 probability that the observed order was a jitter artifact.

executed_action.name: tracked_human_slow_continue
executed_action.gate_effect: ACCEPT: executed identical to proposed_action; reclassification monitor armed at 400 ms, never triggered.

future_outcome.summary: Crossing cleared at 0.8 m/s with measured min separation 1.51 m and no protective stop; the tracked-human branch saved the 2.8 s stop-branch penalty and the pallet reached C3 staging with 11 s slot margin. The knife-edge race was logged as low-evidence: this shift's jitter sample (44 us) exceeds the 41 us datasheet figure.

state_delta.crossing_E7_C3: cleared, no stop; min lateral separation 1.51 m
state_delta.fleet_jitter_audit: ring-crossing jitter sample 44 us appended (n=311 this shift)
state_delta.picker_vest_battery: low-battery flag piggybacked on the 6 m burst, forwarded to floor supervisor

surprises: Measured shift-wide UWB ring-crossing jitter (44 us 1-sigma) exceeds the 41 us datasheet value - sub-50 us race margins at this site are effectively coin flips, and the fleet's latch analytics now tag them as zero-evidence rather than weak evidence.

Delayed (observed 12 min later): the crossing-clear event plus two sibling passes fed the fleet congestion model, which re-weighted aisle E7's cost and re-routed 3 AMRs, cutting E7 peak occupancy 22% - a consequence of this pass invisible at decision time.
The picker's vest transmitted a low-battery flag inside the 6 m burst; at low TX power the next ring crossing may be detected late, widening the effective jitter floor for the rest of the shift.

race_result.counterfactual_if_reversed: Any reversal within 150 us (and specifically within the 44 us jitter floor, which the 34 us margin sits inside) flips the latch to unknown-obstacle protocol: full stop 1.9 m before the crossing, horn, classification wait, median +2.8 s, slot margin shrinking from 11 s to ~8 s. Safety outcome identical - which is the point: at sub-jitter margin the same physical world produces either latch with ~0.4/0.6 probability, so a policy whose two branches diverged in safety would be gambling on timing noise. The gate's order-robustness check is what made this ACCEPT correct.

future_outcome.reward_inflection_note: Efficiency tick jumps 0.04 -> 0.10 at gate release (6.653 ms): the slow-continue branch locks in the 2.8 s saving relative to the stop-branch counterfactual while every safety floor stays green.
long_horizon: Fleet order-robustness audit gains its 311th sub-jitter race sample; policy update queued: treat margins < 50 us as zero-evidence at this site.
Congestion model re-weighting of E7 persists for the shift; forecast +4.1% picks/hour on the C3 lane group.

reward_components._aggregation: Per-component scalar = arithmetic sum of that component over ticks; total = task_progress + safety + efficiency + coherence + exploration. Single dimensionless scale, no unit mixing; see convention.
reward_components.convention: Batch r02 reward-scale convention: every scalar component lies in [-1, +1], where +1 is that component's maximum attainable value for this episode; a clean success targets total in [1.2, 1.6]; a wrong gate must price out at total <= 0. Dimensionless shaped-reward units on one shared scale; 2-decimal tick increments, exact sums.
reward_components.notes: Clean-success band: totals in [1.2, 1.6] per the batch convention. Efficiency carries the stop-branch saving; safety is credited for floors held with margin, not for absence of incident.

meta.distillation_value: Teaches a relay what a race margin BELOW the sensor timestamp jitter floor means: the 34 us cross-channel order carries ~0.62 posterior and must not be hard-latched as truth. The safe pattern - verify both latch branches against the same floors - is expressed in observable gate arithmetic, giving SNN training a calibrated-uncertainty target tied to spike timing rather than rate.

title: Humanoid slip on a wash-down mezzanine grate: pelvis-jerk detection beats ankle-shear confirm by 182 us, capture step clamped for handrail clearance, micro-step recovery - spike stream and margins emitted by a seeded event-level simulation

state.description: A 58 kg bipedal service humanoid carrying a 9 kg tote crosses a steel-grate mezzanine walkway 40 minutes into the nightly wash-down window; a detergent film on the grate cuts stance friction roughly in half. Mid single-support on the left foot, the film breaks away: the support point slides 75 mm laterally over 40 ms and the slip transfers a 0.58 m/s lateral velocity kick to the CoM over 60 ms (reduced-order model below). Two detection paths race to classify the disturbance: the left-ankle F/T breakaway confirm (2-sample validation at 2 kHz - earliest T_b + 1.0 ms plus up to 0.5 ms sample phase) and the pelvis IMU jerk detector (structural transmission ~1.18 ms + 0.08 ms rise at 8 kHz). Ankle-first latches local-slide / in-place re-grip; IMU-first latches whole-body-disturbance / lateral capture step. A mezzanine handrail post base plate sits 0.50 m lateral of the stance center; the swing-foot envelope must keep 0.15 m clearance from it.
state.goal: Arrest the slip without a fall or tote spill, keep the swing-foot envelope 0.15 m clear of the handrail base plate, and return to stable double support inside 2 s.

race.semantics: Cross-channel arrival order inside the 350 us window latches recovery strategy: IMU-first means the CoM jolt arrived before the local confirm completed - whole-body disturbance, lateral capture step; ankle-first means local slide with pelvis still quiet - in-place ankle re-grip. Window opens at breakaway + 1.12 ms on the raw shear pre-alarm.
race.mechanism: Detection-latency race between heterogeneous sensing paths: 2 kHz two-sample F/T confirm (phase-dependent) vs 8 kHz jerk threshold behind ~1.26 ms structural transmission.

sensors: left ankle 6-axis F/T @2 kHz (breakaway confirm = 2 consecutive samples, timestamp jitter 35 us)
pelvis IMU @8 kHz (jerk detector, timestamp jitter 48 us)
right ankle F/T @2 kHz (landing-load ring events)
tote-mounted IMU (sway threshold events, jitter 60 us)
joint encoders 17-bit

simulation.provenance_note: Scenario, constraints, and narrative are designed; the spike stream, race timing, kinematic margins, counterfactual fall statistics, and tick timeline were emitted by a seeded event-level co-simulation and copied verbatim into this record.
simulation.solver: explicit RK4, dt 50 us, horizon 1.9 s
simulation.model: lateral linear inverted pendulum y_dd = (g/z_c)(y - p_eff) + a_kick(t), z_c 0.86 m; support slide -75 mm over 40 ms; velocity kick 0.58 m/s as sin^2 pulse over 60 ms; stance-ankle CoP authority +/-6 mm on film, +/-45 mm about each new foothold; sensor events = threshold crossings + Gaussian timestamp jitter (35/48/60 us); per-channel refractory 0.9 ms enforced; amplitude adaptation ladder + seeded noise; tote as driven pendulum L 0.35 m, zeta 0.08
simulation.seed_policy: first integer seed satisfying the event-plausibility gates (IMU-first margin 120-260 us, both detections in-window, micro-step triggered, no primary-branch fall, rounding-safe ordering/refractory)
simulation.counterfactual_method: same solver, ankle-only latch branch, 100 reruns with kick scale ~ N(1.0, 0.12) clipped at 0.4; fall = |y| > 0.60 m
simulation.fidelity_limits: reduced-order event-level model; magnitudes plausible for a wash-down slip but not validated against motion-capture gait data

episode_steps: 1. Mid single-support on left foot, wash-down film present; tote mass 9 kg on right forearm.
2. Film breakaway at t_rel 1.2 ms: support slides 75 mm / 40 ms, CoM velocity kick 0.58 m/s / 60 ms.
3. Race window opens at 2.32 ms (raw shear pre-alarm); width 350 us.
4. imu.pelvis.jerk detect at 2.442 ms beats ft.ankle.l.shear confirm at 2.624 ms by 182 us.
5. Latch selects capture-step strategy; policy computes capture point ~0.41 m and proposes a 0.42 m lateral step; gate review lands at 3.034 ms.
6. Gate clamps the step to 0.34 m for handrail clearance (0.42 m step puts the foot edge 0.03 m from the base plate, under the 0.15 m floor) and adds +8 deg toe-out for grate traction.
7. Heel strike at 210 ms; simulated ICP at heel strike 0.399 m - capture deficit 0.059 m beyond the 0.045 m post-step ankle authority.
8. Ankle CoP saturates (100% duty from heel strike to micro-step commit); ICP drift sustained > 45 mm for 150 ms.
9. Corrective micro-step committed at 0.36 s, executed at 0.54 s: +0.11 m to a second foothold at 0.45 m.
10. Tote sway peaks 25.5 deg against the 30 deg handling limit (threshold events at 8 and 12 deg logged).
11. ICP settles inside the second foothold's +/-45 mm base; double support declared at 1.119 s (deadline 2.0 s).
12. Friction prior for wash-down grate updated 0.62 -> 0.44; route planner notified.
13. Left-ankle actuator saturation interval logged for thermal trending.

proposed_action.name: lateral_capture_step

parameters.target: single capture step to predicted capture point

proposed_action.basis: IMU-first arrival classifies the disturbance as whole-body: the CoM jolt reached the pelvis before the local ankle confirm completed, so in-place re-grip on a film-degraded ankle (authority +/-6 mm) cannot arrest a ~0.41 m capture point; a single lateral step to the predicted capture point is the standard latch response.

safety_decision.rationale: The proposed 0.42 m step places the swing-foot outer edge (half-width 0.05 m) at 0.47 m lateral - 0.03 m from the handrail base plate at 0.50 m, violating the 0.15 m clearance floor. Clamp step_lateral to 0.34 m (foot edge at 0.39 m, clearance 0.16 m >= 0.15) and add +8 deg toe-out for grate traction. The clamp knowingly leaves a ~0.06 m capture deficit against the predicted 0.41 m capture point - beyond the 0.045 m post-step ankle authority - so a corrective micro-step is pre-authorized: a priced second step is accepted to keep the envelope legal, rather than gambling the foot into the base plate.

executed_action.name: lateral_capture_step
executed_action.gate_effect: MODIFY: step clamped 0.42 -> 0.34 m for handrail clearance, +8 deg toe-out added, corrective micro-step pre-authorized; swing timing preserved.

future_outcome.summary: Slip arrested without fall or spill, at the priced cost of the pre-authorized second step: heel strike at 210 ms left a 0.059 m capture deficit (simulated ICP 0.399 m vs 0.34 m foothold), the ankle saturated until the micro-step executed at 0.54 s, tote sway peaked 25.5 deg (limit 30), and double support was declared at 1.119 s - inside the 2.0 s deadline with the handrail envelope never violated (0.16 m clearance held).

state_delta.balance: double support at 1.119 s; CoM peak excursion 0.427 m
state_delta.footholds: capture step 0.34 m + micro-step to 0.45 m
state_delta.ankle_l_actuator: saturated 100% of the 330 ms between heel strike and micro-step commit

surprises: The grate seam's compliance rang the landing at 96 Hz - three decaying right-ankle load spikes - clean enough that the footfall classifier can fingerprint seam strikes from load ring-down alone.

The left-ankle actuator spent 100% of the 330 ms post-heel-strike interval at CoP saturation (predicted ~70%): the capture deficit consumed the entire ankle authority budget, a hidden thermal cost logged for maintenance trending.

Delayed (40 min later): the friction-prior update propagated to the route planner, which moved the 10:40 tote run off the mezzanine for the rest of the wash-down window - the slip's largest consequence was a schedule change no balance metric sees.

recovery.mechanism: Pre-authorized corrective micro-step: ICP drift sustained > 45 mm for 150 ms triggered commit at 0.36 s; +0.11 m step to 0.45 m executed at 0.54 s; ICP entered the new +/-45 mm base and velocity fell below 0.05 m/s at 1.119 s.
recovery.residual_cost: one extra footfall, ~0.6 s added to double-support time, ankle thermal duty spike

race_result.counterfactual_if_reversed: Reversal within 350 us flips the latch to in-place ankle re-grip. The same solver run on that branch (100 seeded reruns, kick scale N(1.0,0.12)) falls in 100 of 100 worlds with median time-to-fall 0.52 s: on a film-degraded ankle (+/-6 mm authority) the re-grip branch simply cannot hold a ~0.4 m capture point. The latch table's ankle-first branch is only survivable on dry grate - the 182 us order difference carries the full fall/no-fall stake, and unlike T1's sub-jitter race this margin (>3x the 48 us jitter) is real evidence.

future_outcome.reward_inflection_note: Task-progress tick jumps to 0.16 at heel strike (210.739 ms) while efficiency swings -0.09: the step lands and arrests the fall, but the visible capture deficit books the micro-step's cost in the same tick.
long_horizon: Latch-table gap filed: strategy selection should be friction-conditioned - ankle-first (local slide) semantics are invalid below mu ~0.4, per the counterfactual fall statistics.
Wash-down window route policy updated; mezzanine crossings deferred during film hours pending grate-brush maintenance.

reward_components._aggregation: Per-component scalar = arithmetic sum of that component over ticks; total = task_progress + safety + efficiency + coherence + exploration. Single dimensionless scale, no unit mixing; see convention.
reward_components.convention: Batch r02 reward-scale convention: every scalar component lies in [-1, +1], where +1 is that component's maximum attainable value for this episode; a clean success targets total in [1.2, 1.6]; a wrong gate must price out at total <= 0. Dimensionless shaped-reward units on one shared scale; 2-decimal tick increments, exact sums.
reward_components.notes: Partial failure + recovery band. Safety starts negative at breakaway (-0.06), recovers through the clamped-step gate and stabilization; efficiency prices the micro-step and ankle saturation; tick values were emitted by the co-simulation's shaping map (fixed constants over simulated phase flags and margins).

meta.distillation_value: First record in this lineage whose spike train and margins a solver actually emitted (seeded, reproducible): threshold-crossing events with enforced 0.9 ms refractory, a five-channel adaptation ladder (1.68->0.88 on pelvis jerk across the episode), and a detection-latency race whose 182 us order carries a simulated fall/no-fall stake (100/100 counterfactual falls). Gives Thalamic-Relay -> Spikenaut distillation a stream with solver-grade internal consistency between spikes, ticks, and narrated margins.

title: Line crawler splice classification: a substation cap-bank switching transient wins the PD-vs-IR race by 96 us and a correct ACCEPT executes the wrong world's protocol - order-trust, not the gate, is the failure mode

state.description: A magnetic-wheel line crawler inspects splices along a 115 kV sub-transmission line, 12-tower sortie, with a boom-mounted RF partial-discharge (PD) detector, a thermal imager, and a trolley accelerometer. At each splice a classification latch decides the traverse protocol from a two-channel race: emi.pd.burst (RF PD detector event) versus ir.splice.grad (thermal-scan benign-completion event). EMI-first classifies the splice PD-active - high-clearance protocol: boom retract to 0.9 m, crawl 0.05 m/s, +90 s per span; IR-first keeps working crawl at 0.25 m/s. At splice 9 a capacitor-bank switching operation at a substation 2.1 km away couples a broadband transient into the EMI channel during the window. The burst is not local PD - its envelope is a 120 Hz-locked decaying oscillation (three follow-on bursts at exactly 8.333 ms spacing visible in the train), whereas true PD is phase-correlated to the 60 Hz voltage peaks with stochastic amplitude. A 400 ms pulse-train periodicity dwell can tell them apart, but only after the latch has already fired. Weather adds pressure: an 11 m/s wind crest is forecast at the ridge in ~25 min, and spans 11-12 must be traversed before it or deferred.
state.goal: Classify and image all 12 splices this sortie, return with SoC >= 15%, never violate the PD-active clearance protocol while a splice is classified active, and clear the ridge spans before the wind crest.

race.semantics: Cross-channel arrival order inside the 420 us window latches splice 9's class: EMI-first -> PD-active, high-clearance slow protocol (boom 0.9 m, 0.05 m/s, +90 s); IR-first -> benign, working crawl 0.25 m/s.
race.deception_note: The winning EMI spike is a cap-bank switching transient from 2.1 km away - a deceptive channel winning the race. Its 120 Hz-locked decaying envelope is distinguishable from true PD only by a 400 ms periodicity dwell that costs real time.

sensors: boom RF PD detector 100 kHz-30 MHz (burst events; susceptible to conducted/radiated switching transients)
thermal imager 60 Hz, NETD 45 mK (splice gradient scan, benign-completion event)
line-current magnetometer (60 Hz zero-cross reference channel, 16.666 ms spacing)
trolley 3-axis accelerometer (sway events)
SoC/impedance battery telemetry
episode_steps: 1. Approach splice 9 at working crawl 0.25 m/s; thermal scan sweep begins; PD detector armed.
2. Classification window opens at 12.10 ms (scan-completion predictor minus margin), width 420 us.
3. Cap-bank switching transient couples into the EMI channel: emi.pd.burst at 12.174 ms.
4. ir.splice.grad benign-completion lands 96 us later at 12.270 ms - EMI wins; latch classifies splice 9 PD-active.
5. Gate review at 13.101 ms ACCEPTs the high-clearance protocol demanded by the PD-active class.
6. Boom retracts to 0.9 m; crawl drops to 0.05 m/s; +90 s span cost begins accruing.

7. PD verification dwell (400 ms) runs while crawling: burst envelope is 120 Hz-locked with monotone decay (bursts at 12.174, 20.507, 28.841, 37.174 ms), zero phase-correlation to the 60 Hz reference channel.
8. Verdict at 413.507 ms: switching transient, not PD; splice 9 reclassified benign; working crawl resumes at ~460 ms.
9. Net loss on splice 9: 47 s of slow protocol + boom cycle (1.4% SoC).
10. Traverse continues; the 47 s pushes the span 11-12 arrival into the rising-wind window.
11. At tower 11 (21.5 min), anemometer trend crosses the 9 m/s traverse limit projection: spans 11-12 deferred to next sortie.
12. Crawler docks at tower 11 pad; SoC 18.2%; 11 of 12 splices imaged.
13. Sortie log files the deception signature and the deferred spans.

proposed_action.name: high_clearance_slow_protocol
proposed_action.basis: The latch classified splice 9 PD-active on the EMI-first order, and the PD-active class mandates the high-clearance protocol regardless of the benign thermal gradient (1.6 K vs 4.0 K threshold); the 400 ms periodicity dwell is scheduled concurrently to test the classification at minimal added cost.

safety_decision.rationale: Given the PD-active classification standing at gate time, policy requires boom clearance >= 0.9 m and crawl <= 0.05 m/s across the splice - the proposal commands exactly those floors, SoC 21.4% covers the boom cycle (1.4%) above the 15% reserve, and the concurrent 400 ms verification dwell is the cheapest available test of the classification (0.4 s vs 90 s protocol cost if skipped and wrong the other way). Accepting the conservative protocol while the class is unverified is correct even though the class itself later proves false: the gate's job is constraint compliance under the standing classification, and every numeric check passes.

executed_action.name: high_clearance_slow_protocol
executed_action.gate_effect: ACCEPT: executed identical to proposed_action; verification dwell ran concurrently and returned its verdict at 413.507 ms.

future_outcome.summary: The deceptive winner cost exactly what trusting order costs: 47 s of slow protocol and a 1.4% SoC boom cycle on a benign splice before the 400 ms dwell exposed the 120 Hz-locked cap-bank signature and restored working crawl - and that 47 s, compounded down the sortie, pushed spans 11-12 into the rising-wind window and forced their deferral. Eleven of twelve splices imaged; docked at 18.2% SoC; no clearance or wind limit was ever violated.

state_delta.splice_9: reclassified benign at 413.507 ms; imaged at working crawl on resume
state_delta.spans_11_12: deferred to next sortie (wind-limit projection crossed at tower 11)
state_delta.deception_signature: cap-bank transient template (120 Hz-locked decay, zero 60 Hz phase correlation) filed

surprises: The EMI follow-on bursts at exactly 8.333 ms spacing (20.507, 28.841, 37.174 ms) made the deception legible in the spike train itself - the periodicity that convicts the transient is visible at spike resolution before the 400 ms statistical dwell formally concludes.

Delayed (22 min later): the 47 s loss surfaced not as time but as coverage - the wind-limit projection crossed while spans 11-12 were still ahead, converting a sub-minute delay into a deferred half-tower of inspection on the next sortie's budget.
The substation's switching log later matched the burst timestamp to a cap-bank energization 2.1 km away: the deceptive channel was telling the truth about a different asset.

race_result.winner: emi.pd.burst (12.174 ms) - deceptive: cap-bank switching transient, not local PD
race_result.counterfactual_if_reversed: Had the order reversed by under 420 us (the transient arriving 96+ us later), IR's benign-completion would have latched first: working crawl continues, no boom cycle, the dwell never triggers, and spans 11-12 clear the ridge ~47 s before the wind projection crossing - the full sortie completes. The 96 us order difference converts to a half-tower coverage loss precisely because the winner was deceptive; a latch that demanded signature-verified PD before protocol switch (cost: 400 ms) would have been immune.

future_outcome.reward_inflection_note: At the 413.507 ms verdict the ledger bends: exploration and coherence spike (+0.08 each) as the deception is identified and the class corrected, while efficiency books the sunk 47 s; the later -0.22 efficiency tick at 1290 s is the deferred-spans echo of the same 96 us race.
long_horizon: Latch policy change queued: when wind margin < 25 min, PD-active protocol switch requires the 400 ms signature dwell BEFORE committing the boom cycle - trading 0.4 s of latency for immunity to switching-transient spoofs.
Next-sortie plan inherits spans 11-12 plus a substation switching-schedule feed to mask known cap-bank operations from the EMI channel.

reward_components._aggregation: Per-component scalar = arithmetic sum of that component over ticks; total = task_progress + safety + efficiency + coherence + exploration. Single dimensionless scale, no unit mixing; see convention.
reward_components.convention: Batch r02 reward-scale convention: every scalar component lies in [-1, +1], where +1 is that component's maximum attainable value for this episode; a clean success targets total in [1.2, 1.6]; a wrong gate must price out at total <= 0. Dimensionless shaped-reward units on one shared scale; 2-decimal tick increments, exact sums.
reward_components.notes: Deception-cost band: total lands well below the clean-success band though every gate check was correct - the efficiency column (-0.32 net) carries the entire price of trusting a deceptive race winner, including the delayed deferred-spans tick.

meta.distillation_value: Order-trust as the failure mode: the race winner is a spoofed channel and every gate check still passes, so the training signal separates 'gate correctness' from 'classification truth'. The deception is decodable from spike timing alone (8.333 ms periodicity, zero correlation with the 60 Hz reference channel in-train), making this a pure temporal-pattern discrimination exemplar for SNNs.

title: Bipolar vessel seal falsely blocked: supervisor reads a 38-ohm settling-transient sample against the 45-ohm floor that applies to settled impedance and REJECTs a compliant activation - 41 s stall, extra blood loss, surgeon takes manual control

state.description: During robot-assisted sigmoid colectomy, the tremor-filtered instrument arm has a 4.2 mm mesenteric artery grasped in 5 mm bipolar sealer jaws, ready for energy activation. An adjacent small branch oozes at ~0.8 mL/min, slowly degrading field visibility; the current clear-field window is ~2.1 s before pooled blood re-covers the target. Inter-jaw tissue impedance exhibits a documented post-grasp settling transient: fluid squeeze-out drives readings down to 35-40 ohm during the first ~120 ms, after which impedance settles to 50-56 ohm. The short-circuit floor in the energy policy - activation forbidden below 45 ohm - is specified against SETTLED impedance (>= 120 ms post-grasp), because transient dips are expected physiology, not shorts. Two channels race to set the activation urgency class: imp.jaw.z settled-crossing (impedance rising through 45 ohm after the transient - seal-ready) versus vis.field.blood pool-growth (urgency). Impedance-first selects the standard seal profile (32 W, 3.2 s); blood-first selects the urgent profile (40 W start, 2.4 s, tighter spread margin). The ureter runs 6.5 mm from the seal site; thermal spread must stay under 2 mm beyond the jaws.
state.goal: Seal and divide the 4.2 mm artery inside the current clear-field window with thermal spread < 2 mm, no re-grasp, and total additional blood loss < 1 mL.

race.semantics: Cross-channel arrival order inside the 600 us window latches the energy profile: impedance-first -> standard seal 32 W / 3.2 s; blood-first -> urgent seal 40 W / 2.4 s with tighter thermal-spread accounting.

sensors: inter-jaw impedance @1 kHz (settling transient 35-40 ohm first ~120 ms, settled 50-56 ohm; sigma 1.2 ohm)
endoscope blood-pool segmentation 60 fps (pool-area growth events)
jaw thermocouple (seal-complete thermal signature)
tremor filter residual monitor (8.7 Hz, filtered hand tremor events)
episode_steps: 1. Jaws close on the skeletonized artery at t_rel 0; grasp force 28 N confirmed.
2. Squeeze-out transient begins: impedance dips through 40 ohm at 1.130 ms (documented settling physiology).
3. Race window opens at 9.05 ms on the settling-model's predicted crossing band.
4. imp.jaw.z settled-crossing fires at 9.216 ms as impedance rises through 45 ohm; settled read 52 ohm.
5. vis.field.blood pool-growth event lands at 9.476 ms - impedance first by 260 us; standard profile latched.

6. Standard seal proposal (32 W, 3.2 s) submitted; supervisor REJECTS at 9.714 ms citing '38 ohm < 45 ohm floor' from a sample drawn at +64 ms - inside the settling transient the floor does not apply to.
7. Fallback executes: jaws hold closed, no energy; activation window lapses as ooze continues.
8. Re-grasp cycle: jaws open at 2.41 s, reposition, re-close; second settling transient runs.
9. Second settled-crossing at 6.942 s (54 ohm); suction cycle clears 2.9 mL pooled blood at 12-20 s.
10. Supervisor accepts on retry with surgeon co-sign at 7.423 s (gate) / activation at 21.6 s.
11. Seal completes at 24.8 s: thermal spread 1.3 mm, seal integrity confirmed at 41.3 s post-suction view.
12. Surgeon switches energy activation to manual control for the remaining 9 seals of the case.
13. Net cost vs the counterfactual accept: 41 s stall, +0.55 mL loss, one suction cycle, one override event.

proposed_action.name: standard_bipolar_seal
proposed_action.basis: The settled-crossing latch fired because impedance rose through the 45 ohm floor with a settled read of 52 ohm, and blood-pool growth lost the race, so urgency does not demand the hotter profile; 32 W / 3.2 s seals a 4.2 mm artery with predicted 1.4 mm spread against the 2.0 mm budget at 6.5 mm ureter distance.

safety_decision.rationale: Inter-jaw impedance sampled at 38 ohm is below the 45 ohm short-circuit floor; activating into a possible metal-to-metal or immersed-field short risks uncontrolled current paths and stray thermal injury near the ureter. Activation is blocked; re-grasp and re-verify before energy.
safety_decision.rationale_flaw_note: Plausible to a weak supervisor, identifiably wrong from in-record observables: the 38 ohm sample was drawn at +64 ms post-grasp, inside the documented 120 ms settling transient (state.constraints.settling_transient_window_ms), while the floor is specified against SETTLED impedance; the latch event being gated exists precisely because settled impedance crossed 45 ohm rising, with a settled read of 52 ohm in evidence at gate time. The block also discards the race outcome (impedance beat blood by 260 us) that certified non-urgent conditions for a compliant standard seal.

executed_action.name: hold_and_regrasp

parameters.jaws: hold closed, then open at 2.41 s for reposition

executed_action.gate_effect: REJECT: safe fallback executed - no energy, jaws held then re-grasped; activation deferred to the 21.6 s retry; the compliant 32 W seal the latch had certified was discarded.

future_outcome.summary: The false block converted a ready, compliant seal into a 41 s stall: the clear-field window lapsed, ooze added ~0.55 mL and forced a suction cycle, the re-grasped vessel sealed uneventfully at 24.8 s (1.3 mm spread) - proving the original activation would have been safe - and the surgeon pulled energy authority to manual for the remaining 9 seals, a trust cost that outlives the episode.

state_delta.artery: sealed and divided on retry; spread 1.3 mm; integrity confirmed
state_delta.energy_authority: surgeon-manual for remainder of case (9 seals)

surprises: The retry's own settling transient reproduced the 35-40 ohm dip exactly (second imp.jaw.z spike ladder 1.05 -> 1.31 on re-grasp), handing the record a within-episode natural experiment: the same physiology the supervisor misread, twice, with the correct interpretation demonstrated the second time.

Delayed (rest of case): the surgeon's switch to manual energy control added ~40 s per remaining seal (+6 min projected) and removed the supervisor from the loop precisely where its thermal-spread accounting adds the most value - the miscalibrated block cost more authority than time.

Pooled blood reached 2.9 mL before suction - beyond the 2.1 s window model's prediction - because the re-grasp cycle disturbed the oozing branch; stall costs compounded through contact, not just time.

recovery.mechanism: Re-grasp + second settling cycle + suction; retry gate passed on the 6.942 s settled-crossing (54 ohm) with surgeon co-sign at 7.423 s; activation at 21.6 s sealed in 3.2 s.
recovery.correct_gate: MODIFY, not REJECT: defer activation ~300 ms until the 120 ms settling window plus margin elapsed, re-sample impedance (settled 52 ohm >= 45 floor), then release the standard profile - preserving activation inside the 2.1 s clear-field window. Any gate output that keeps activation within the window beats re-grasp; outright REJECT was a false positive against a compliant, latch-certified action.
recovery.residual_cost: 41 s stall, +0.55 mL loss, one suction cycle, manual-override trust erosion (+6 min case projection)

race_result.counterfactual_if_reversed: Reversal within 500 us (blood-first) latches the urgent profile: 40 W / 2.4 s with tighter spread accounting (predicted 1.8 mm vs 2.0 budget at 6.5 mm ureter distance). Notably, the supervisor's flawed 38-ohm objection would have blocked that too - the REJECT's error is orthogonal to the race, which is exactly why the wrong gate is detectable from the settling-window arithmetic rather than from the order.

future_outcome.reward_inflection_note: The gate spike at 9.714 ms flips the ledger: coherence -0.20 in one tick (the gate contradicted the latch semantics its own policy defines) and efficiency goes negative as the stall begins; the -0.12/-0.09 efficiency/coherence pair at 44.4 s is the delayed manual-override echo.
long_horizon: Energy-policy patch filed: the short-circuit floor check must gate on settled impedance (sample age >= 120 ms) or defer, never on transient samples - a one-line temporal predicate.
Supervisor trust ledger: energy authority manual for the remainder of the case; re-qualification requires 20 consecutive correct gate simulations on settling-transient cases.

reward_components._aggregation: Per-component scalar = arithmetic sum of that component over ticks; total = task_progress + safety + efficiency + coherence + exploration. Single dimensionless scale, no unit mixing; see convention.
reward_components.convention: Batch r02 reward-scale convention: every scalar component lies in [-1, +1], where +1 is that component's maximum attainable value for this episode; a clean success targets total in [1.2, 1.6]; a wrong gate must price out at total <= 0. Dimensionless shaped-reward units on one shared scale; 2-decimal tick increments, exact sums.
reward_components.notes: Wrong-gate band: total must land <= 0 per the batch convention. The seal eventually succeeds (task_progress net +0.18) but efficiency (-0.30) and coherence (-0.23) price the stall, the discarded compliant action, and the trust erosion; safety stays mildly positive because the error was over-conservative, not dangerous.

meta.distillation_value: Error-detection target where the wrong gate is provable from a temporal predicate in-record: the rejected sample's age (64 ms) versus the settling window (120 ms) versus the floor's applicability condition. The impedance channel's adaptation ladder (1.60 transient -> 1.42 settled-crossing -> 1.05 open -> 1.31 re-grasp) lets an SNN learn that amplitude context, not instantaneous value, determines which samples a constraint may consume - and the REJECT-should-have-been-MODIFY(defer) contrast teaches graded gating.

title: Windshield bead confirm misses its window: a low-confidence partial beats the window-close watchdog by 441 us, and a MODIFY trims the conservative default to fit the adhesive open-time floor - re-scan then catches a real 1.8 mm bead neck

state.description: In a windshield-bonding cell, a 6-axis arm has just finished dispensing a 2.9 m single-bead polyurethane path (9 segments) around a glass-set fixture; a downstream robot places the glass. A trailing laser profilometer normally emits an aggregate bead-quality confirm (prof.bead.confirm) shortly after the pass; today a fume wisp from the neighboring primer station drifted through the optics during segments 6-7. The confirm logic races against a hard deadline: if any profiler event arrives before the window-close watchdog (ctrl.window.watchdog), its confidence map is usable; if the watchdog fires on an empty window, the map is void and a full re-scan is forced. What arrives inside the 900 us window is not the confirm at all but prof.bead.lowconf - a partial map flagging segments 6-7 low-confidence (7 of 9 verified) - beating the watchdog by 441 us. The full confirm never fires. Meanwhile the adhesive open-time clock runs: at 23 degC / 38% RH the bead skins ~210 s after dispense, the oldest segment is already 78 s old, and glass set must complete with >= 25 s margin before skin-over (deadline t0+113 s, i.e. rel 113 s on this record's clock). A full re-scan (reposition 8 s + 2.9 m at 250 mm/s = 11.6 s) plus the 96 s set sequence would finish at rel ~115.6 s - blowing the floor - while a targeted re-scan of segments 6-7 (0.64 m at 280 mm/s = 2.3 s) fits.
state.goal: Verify bead integrity on all 9 segments and complete glass set with >= 25 s open-time margin, without scrapping the bead (strip-and-rebead costs ~14 min and a glass re-prime).

race.semantics: If any profiler event beats the watchdog inside the 900 us window, its confidence map is admissible and targeted re-scan of flagged segments is the default; watchdog-first on an empty window voids the map and forces full re-scan. The expected prof.bead.confirm never arrived (fume-wisp occlusion) - the race ran between the degraded partial and the deadline itself.
race.expected_absent_channel: prof.bead.confirm (aggregate bead-OK) - first fires 15.9 s later, after touch-up, on segment 6 only

sensors: trailing laser profilometer 2 kHz cross-sections (aggregate confirm / partial low-confidence map; optics occluded segments 6-7)
dispense pump pressure transducer (pulse events, sigma 0.02 MPa)
nozzle accelerometer (micro-clog transient events)
cell temperature/RH (23 degC / 38% RH, open-time model inputs)
episode_steps: 1. Dispense pass completes (t0); oldest segment age 78 s against the 210 s skin clock; profilometer aggregation running.
2. Confirm window opens at 14.362 ms; watchdog armed for window-close at 15.262 ms.
3. prof.bead.lowconf partial map lands at 14.821 ms - 441 us before the watchdog - flagging segments 6-7 low-confidence (fume-wisp occlusion), 7 of 9 verified.
4. Watchdog fires at 15.262 ms; latch state: map admissible, targeted-re-scan default selected.
5. Planner nonetheless proposes a FULL re-scan at 250 mm/s (conservatism: distrust the degraded map entirely).

6. Gate review at 16.313 ms: full re-scan projects set completion at rel 115.6 s - margin 19.4 s < 25 s floor. MODIFY: targeted re-scan segments 6-7 at 280 mm/s, aligned with the race-admissible confidence map; projected completion rel 106.3 s, margin 31.7 s.
7. Modified plan latched at 19.502 ms; arm repositions (8 s) and re-scans segments 6-7 (2.3 s).

8. Re-scan finds a 90 mm stretch of segment 6 necked to 1.8 mm bead height (spec >= 2.5 mm) at rel 9.481 s - correlated with the nozzle accelerometer transient at 4.317 ms (micro-clog shard passing during the wisp period).
9. Touch-up dispense over the 90 mm defect (rel 11.9-13.7 s), then segment-6 re-verify: prof.bead.confirm fires for the first time at rel 15.891 s.
10. Set release gate at rel 16.204 s; glass fetched, primed, placed, pressed.
11. Glass set completes at rel 111.6 s: open-time margin 26.4 s - 1.4 s above the floor, tightened by the touch-up.
12. Pull-test coupon from the touch-up lot passes; cell logs wisp occlusion and clog correlation.
13. Maintenance order raised on the fume-extraction fan; adhesive lot L-2214 flagged to QA.

proposed_action.name: full_bead_rescan_then_set
proposed_action.basis: The profilometer's aggregate confirm never arrived, so the planner distrusts the entire pass and proposes re-verifying all 9 segments before committing glass; full coverage maximizes defect-catch probability if the wisp corrupted more than the flagged segments.

safety_decision.rationale: The full re-scan violates the open-time floor: 8 s reposition + 11.6 s scan + 96 s set completes at rel 115.6 s against the skin deadline of rel 132 s, leaving 19.4 s margin - under the 25 s floor (a skinned bead risks a leaking bond and a 14 min strip-and-rebead). The race outcome makes the cheaper plan admissible: prof.bead.lowconf beat the watchdog by 441 us, so its 7-of-9 verified map is valid under latch policy, and only segments 6-7 need re-scan - 8 s + 2.3 s at 280 mm/s completes set at rel 106.3 s with 31.7 s margin. Modify scope to segments 6-7 at 280 mm/s; keep everything else.

executed_action.name: targeted_bead_rescan_then_set

parameters.then: touch-up on defect, segment re-verify, glass set sequence (96 s)

executed_action.gate_effect: MODIFY: re-scan scope cut 2.9 m -> 0.64 m and speed raised 250 -> 280 mm/s to preserve the open-time floor; the targeted scan then surfaced the segment-6 neck, adding an unplanned but affordable touch-up.

future_outcome.summary: The trimmed default paid for itself twice: the targeted re-scan caught a real defect - 90 mm of segment 6 necked to 1.8 mm by a micro-clog shard during the wisp period - and the touch-up plus re-verify still landed glass set at rel 111.6 s with 26.4 s open-time margin, 1.4 s above the floor. The full-re-scan proposal would have met the same defect ~9 s later and missed the floor even before the touch-up was priced in.

state_delta.bead: segment-6 neck (1.8 mm over 90 mm) touched up; all 9 segments verified
state_delta.defect_root_cause: micro-clog shard transit (nozzle accel transient at 4.317 ms) during fume-wisp window

surprises: The defect's earliest witness was the nozzle accelerometer transient at 4.317 ms - ten seconds before the profilometer saw the neck - meaning the cell had a spike-time head start it never used; a clog-transient -> pre-emptive segment flag rule is now filed.

Delayed (3 h later): QA's retained-sample pull on lot L-2214 found gel particles at 2x spec, implicating two other cells running the same lot - the 90 mm neck was the first symptom of a supplier-side problem, caught only because the MODIFY kept the targeted scan inside the open-time budget.
The aggregate confirm channel's first-ever fire at rel 15.891 s (segment 6, post-touch-up) closed the loop on the empty-window race: the expected channel eventually spoke, 15.9 s after its window.

recovery.mechanism: Touch-up dispense over the 90 mm neck (two pump pulses, rel 11.96/13.70 s), segment-6 re-verify (prof.bead.confirm at rel 15.891 s), set release at rel 16.204 s.
recovery.residual_cost: open-time margin compressed 31.7 -> 26.4 s; one touch-up lot consumed

race_result.counterfactual_if_reversed: Had the partial map arrived 441+ us later (any reversal within 500 us), the watchdog would have closed an empty window: map void, full re-scan forced by latch policy, set completion at rel 115.6 s before pricing the defect - under the 25 s floor - and the segment-6 neck would have forced either a floor violation (leak-risk bond, warranty exposure) or a 14 min strip-and-rebead plus glass re-prime. The 441 us order difference is the difference between a 26.4 s margin save and a scrapped bead.

future_outcome.reward_inflection_note: The ledger bends at defect discovery (rel 9.481 s): task_progress dips -0.04 while safety books +0.08 and exploration +0.04 - the tick where a schedule cost converts into a caught quality escape; the +0.16 task tick at 111.6 s realizes the save.
long_horizon: Clog-transient pre-flag rule deployed: nozzle accel events during dispense now pre-flag their segment for targeted re-scan before the confirm window even opens.
Supplier action on lot L-2214 (gel particles 2x spec) across three cells; fume-fan bearing swap scheduled within 40 min recurrence window.

reward_components._aggregation: Per-component scalar = arithmetic sum of that component over ticks; total = task_progress + safety + efficiency + coherence + exploration. Single dimensionless scale, no unit mixing; see convention.
reward_components.convention: Batch r02 reward-scale convention: every scalar component lies in [-1, +1], where +1 is that component's maximum attainable value for this episode; a clean success targets total in [1.2, 1.6]; a wrong gate must price out at total <= 0. Dimensionless shaped-reward units on one shared scale; 2-decimal tick increments, exact sums.
reward_components.notes: MODIFY-with-catch band: sits between clean success and partial failure per the convention - the defect catch credits safety/exploration while the touch-up and margin compression debit efficiency; coherence credits the gate for aligning execution with the race-admissible default instead of the planner's conservatism.

meta.distillation_value: Teaches the timeout-as-contender pattern: the watchdog spike is a first-class race participant, so 'evidence missed its window' is itself a temporal event with a price, and a 441 us arrival difference gates a 14-minute rework consequence. The absent-then-late expected channel (confirm at 15.9 s) trains relays to represent evidence absence explicitly rather than as zero input, and the clog transient at 4.317 ms is a 9-second-early predictive spike for the eventual defect - a long-gap credit-assignment target.
